h: Round Off a Night in the Merchant City
p: You can't miss George Square, and the grand Glasgow City Chambers that sit along its east side are one of the city's most impressive buildings. Its marble staircases and ornate halls are famous, and it's worth keeping an eye out for any public tours running while you're in town. From there, a short walk takes you up to Glasgow Cathedral, a magnificent medieval building that survived the Reformation largely intact, and the Necropolis on the hill behind it, a Victorian cemetery with sweeping views over the city.

For your darts session, a bit of planning helps. Book the right number of players and arrive a few minutes early so you can grab a drink and settle in. If you've got a big group, split into teams across two oches so nobody's waiting around too long for their turn.

Never thrown a dart in your life? No bother. Stand side-on to the board with your front foot forward, keep your elbow still and use your forearm to throw. Smooth and steady is the way to go. The scoring tech takes care of the maths, so all you need to worry about is the aim.

Glasgow is famous for its nightlife and its friendliness, and a darts session fits right in. Afterwards, the Merchant City's bars and restaurants are all around you, and live music venues are dotted across the city if you fancy keeping the night going. Glasgow rarely does early nights.
